metadata.case_name: DAYAWON FE BATIANCILA v. CHIEN CHI TOEPKER

source: Physical examination noted redness and tenderness, pain and limitation on motion of her shoulder and back. There was no sensory deficit. Results of neurological examination were within normal limits. The diagnosis was right shoulder and back injuries.
injuries.icd_description: Contusion of lower back or pelvis

injuries.description: right shoulder contusion / right shoulder injury
source: Physical examination noted redness and tenderness, pain and limitation on motion of her shoulder and back. There was no sensory deficit. Results of neurological examination were within normal limits. The diagnosis was right shoulder and back injuries.

Physical examination at the Orthopaedics Department showed diminished power over right leg due to back pain. Sphincter function was intact. Right shoulder range of motion was full except a mild limitation in active flexion and extension due to pain.
injuries.icd_description: Contusion of shoulder or upper arm

manifestations.description: numbness on right shoulder radiated to her neck
difficulty in prolonged walking and standing; could not walk fast or sit still for long time
difficulty changing position in bed and getting up from bed
difficulty in holding pen or pencil to write
reduced range of motion of right shoulder (mild limitation in active flexion and extension; forward flexion limited to 140 degrees)
required walking aid (frame / walking stick) for support in ward and for a period during treatment
bruise over the lower back and the right upper back, both with tenderness

treatments_received.treatment: attendance at Top Medical Health Center (out-patient) on 21 June 2010
source: DFB attended the Top Medical Health Center on 21 June 2010, ie the date of the alleged accident, for treatment.

treatments_received.treatment: attendance at A&E of Queen Elizabeth Hospital on 23 and 26 June 2010
source: DFB attended A&E of QEH on 23 and 26 June 2010.

treatments_received.treatment: admission to Orthopaedics Department of Queen Elizabeth Hospital (26 June 2010 to 30 June 2010)
source: She was admitted to the Orthopaedics Department of QEH on 26 June 2010 and discharged on 30 June 2010.

treatments_received.treatment: physiotherapy (attended Physiotherapy Department of QEH for sessions; exercises and modalities provided)
source: She also attended the Physiotherapy Department of QEH for two sessions.

She was initially assessed by the Physiotherapy Department of QEH on 7 September 2010. ... She was given Interferential Therapy and Hot Pack to relieve back and neck symptoms. Back and neck exercises were prescribed with back and neck care advice.

losses.description: Difficulty in prolonged walking and standing; required walking aid (frame / walking stick) for support during treatment; could not walk fast or sit still for long time.
